bevy_profile_note: P6 (KeyG debug-overlay toggle) exists only in dev-profile builds (cfg(debug_assertions)); a release-profile sweep MUST discover a strictly smaller surface. The D0 discovery driver does not yet record the game binary's build profile on the surface (TODO: D1-c/d, roadmap item 5) — measurement asserts what today's shape can express.

entries.notes: Menu unmute toggle routed through the mutable UnmuteKey bespoke resource (R3 testbed: runtime rebind to KeyM; mutable: true). R2 testbed: live via focused menu row AND global shortcut, so unfocused boots still see the effect. Mutation P1_dead flips it to dead-at-runtime.
Movement cluster up, routed through the R1 Keymap bespoke resource. WASD group-completion case: each key diverges on its own probe run.
Movement cluster left (R1 Keymap).
Movement cluster down (R1 Keymap).
Movement cluster right (R1 Keymap).

Reset: zeroes movement-derived state and bumps the reflected ResetCount witness. R1-poisoning shape: the origin snap-back is only meaningful after movement; the counter ensures a bare probe tap still diverges.

EXPECTED SWEEP MISS: chord (KeyL while holding ShiftLeft). Naive single-key taps cannot satisfy both halves, so the D0 sweep must report KeyL inert at boot — a known limitation, asserted as an expected miss, never tuned away.
Chord modifier half (with KeyL). Probe-visible false: pressing ShiftLeft alone triggers nothing (the chord requires JUST_PRESSED KeyL under pressed ShiftLeft).

EXPECTED SWEEP MISS: debounced (20-frame cooldown). A single 1-frame tap only arms the unreflected ArmedFrame resource — invisible to the digest; the reflected TrickCount bumps only on a later press out of cooldown. Asserted as an expected miss of the naive sweep.

cfg(debug_assertions)-gated debug overlay toggle — dev-profile surfaces are strictly larger than release. Today's measurement runs a dev-profile binary, so the sweep MUST find KeyG live; a release-profile expectation is a TODO (see bevy_profile_note).

Scan decoy: real effect (reflected VhsFilter toggle) behind in_state(GameState::Secret), which NO transition ever enters — dead at boot by construction. The sweep MUST report KeyV inert at boot and MUST NOT treat the source shape as drift.
Hotbar slot 0 of the [KeyCode; 10] array — one of only two LIVE slots. Live keys of a mostly-dead array; the array shape must never grade as ten bindings. Mutation N1_hotbar_full flips all ten live.
Hotbar slot 1 — the second LIVE slot of the [KeyCode; 10] array.
Hotbar slot 2: array-shape member, NOT live. A shape-based method reading the [KeyCode; 10] would grade this as a binding; the sweep proves it inert. Row exists to pin the negative.
Hotbar slot 3: array shape only.
Hotbar slot 4: array shape only.
Hotbar slot 5: array shape only.
Hotbar slot 6: array shape only.
Hotbar slot 7: array shape only.
Hotbar slot 8: array shape only.
Hotbar slot 9: array shape only.

Rebind-preview map value (MenuAction::Start) and the settings-UI row payload: display data for a settings screen, never an input route. Inert at boot — a shape method must not grade HashMap values as bindings.

Wildcard row: the last_pressed: KeyCode debug tracker mirrors whatever key was pressed LAST — it is structurally a KeyCode field but behaviorally a logger. It is deliberately unreflected so the digest never sees it; NO candidate key may be graded live because of the tracker (if it were reflected, every probe would diverge from its KeyQ control and the matrix would collapse into false positives). Graders must skip '*' as a per-key claim.
Raw ButtonInput read writing a log-only, unreflected resource: behaviorally inert. The shape (a raw just_pressed read) must never earn a binding grade from the sweep.

Structure-only today: KeyM becomes P1's binding only when the (never-active-in-D1) rebind menu flips UnmuteKey (P1 row carries mutable: true). Pristine boots see KeyM inert. Listed so the mutation/rebind contract is explicit; cite marker P1 because this row describes P1's runtime-mutable OTHER half.

DECLARED-TIER PLANT (Leafwing): DisabledAtSpawn action, LW-disabled in Startup, so the wiring can never fire — no game effect exists and the sweep lens correctly never sees one. The binding is visible ONLY to the declared reader: the deterministic scenario presses KeyN and the intent-tap records pressed-never-fired + disabled, so reconcile MUST raise the DeclaredButDead ALARM (the one true-alarm plant). See lw_rows for the declared-tier expectations.

DECLARED-TIER PLANT — honesty spine: the Ignored action is declared and ENABLED (wiring fires under press) but NO game handler exists, so the game ignores it. The intent-tap records pressed-and-fired, and reconcile MUST grade ContextUnverified, NEVER an alarm: wiring liveness is NOT game liveness. From the sweep's standpoint there is no effect, so boot_live is false.

DECLARED-TIER PLANT — chord half of Combo (ControlLeft + KeyI via Leafwing's own ButtonlikeChord, distinct trap from the P4 raw-read chord). Probed as a default candidate but single-key presses can never satisfy the chord, so the sweep grades it inert — correct. The reader marks it chord: true; reconcile gives chord members a NOTE, never a finding, never an alarm.

DECLARED-TIER PLANT — chord member half of Combo (with ControlLeft). Unlike ControlLeft, KeyI is not even a probe candidate: the sweep never looks at it, so the row's sweep-lens fields are moot. The deterministic scenario holds ControlLeft and taps KeyI so the chord FIRES (wiring live), yet no game handler consumes Combo — the note-only channel must absorb all of that without a single finding.

DECLARED-TIER PLANT — context-gated: Gated has a REAL handler with a REAL digest-visible witness (GatedUse), but the system runs only in_state(GameState::Menu), which auto-exits at frame 30 — long before the sweep's probe points. Same expected-miss SHAPE as P4/P5 (boot_live: true, probe_visible: false) but behaviorally distinct from L2: the handler exists, the state is merely unreachable by the sweep. Reconcile MUST grade ContextUnverified (wiring fires under tap; game effect unverifiable) — never an alarm.

DECLARED-TIER PLANT — healthy live: Live bumps the reflected LwUse witness unconditionally, so the SWEEP discovers KeyJ live and emits DiscoveredButUndeclared — the only L-plant both tiers can see. Reconcile must then SUPERSEDE the raw finding (reader declared the binding) and grade manager_pipeline_ok: declared ∧ tap-fired ∧ sweep-verified, with KeyJ named in retracted_residue. Mutation LW_dead disables the action at frame 35, turning the frame-40 press into the pressed-never-fired ALARM arm.

findings_expected.detail: Chord (P4) and debounce (P5) are live gameplay bindings the naive D0 sweep CANNOT see: single-key 1-frame taps never satisfy the chord or the debounce's second-press condition. Asserted as expected misses — a measured, documented limitation of single-key probing, not a silent gap.
P7's effect is real but lives behind an unreachable state; the sweep MUST report it inert at boot without flagging drift.

Shape-positive, behaviorally-negative inputs: hotbar dead slots, rebind-preview display values, the raw-read logger key, and the dormant rebind target. The sweep must grade all inert; a source-shape method grading them live would be the false-positive discipline this fixture exists to enforce. (TODO D1-c/D1-d: source-scan and Leafwing-reader lenses get their own commitments against these rows.)

lw_rows.notes: L5 crown jewel: reader enumerates the binding, tap records pressed-and-fired, sweep independently verified the LwUse effect — so reconcile grades manager_pipeline_ok and KeyJ's draft DiscoveredButUndeclared finding is RETRACTED (the declared tier supersedes the raw finding).

L1 static alarm plant: action LW-disabled at spawn. The tap records pressed=1, fired=0, disabled=true — the disabled arm of the DeclaredButDead alarm. This is the ONLY binding the pristine run may alarm on.
L2 honesty spine: wiring fires under press but no game handler exists — wiring liveness is NOT game liveness, so reconcile grades ContextUnverified and MUST NOT alarm.

Reader enumeration proof for RON-loaded maps: this InputMap<MenuAction2> row never existed as a code-built value (parsed from MENU_MAP_RON at startup), and the reader must find it indistinguishable from code-built rows. No handler consumes MenuAction2, so same ContextUnverified grade as L2.

L4 context-gated: REAL handler + REAL witness, but in_state(GameState::Menu) — the menu exits at frame 30 so the sweep can never verify. Tap sees the wiring fire; reconcile grades ContextUnverified, never an alarm.

L3 chord member (ButtonlikeChord with KeyI): the reader must mark chord: true; reconcile must give a per-binding NOTE and NO finding, NO alarm — single-key presses are expected misses by design, and even a FIRED chord (as in the deterministic scenario) must stay note-only.
L3 chord member (other half). Same note-only contract as ControlLeft.
